Subject: Marketplace private offer unit price mapping

Thanks again for taking the time today, Brian — great conversation. Per our discovery, here’s a short recap and the asks I promised on pricing/unit economics so your procurement team can evaluate marketplace private offers (AWS/GCP/Azure) vs. direct Redwood billing.

Recap (from our call):
- Estimated monthly token volume: 180M - 250M tokens (grows to ~1.2B tokens by Q3 next year)
- Current target budget range: $120k - $180k annual committed spend (customer indicated they can stretch if unit economics justify)
- Primary marketplaces under consideration: AWS Marketplace (Gov and Commercial), Azure Marketplace, GCP Marketplace
- Decision drivers: unit $/1M tokens, marketplace fees + markup, contract term (12 vs 24 months), PO/Private Offer support and procurement timelines

What we need from BrightCart:
1) Confirm an expected month-1 and month-6 token run-rate (we used 200M/mo as a working number today)
2) Confirm whether procurement wants pricing routed strictly through marketplace private offer (preferred for their internal procurement) or a hybrid (marketplace for purchase + direct invoicing for support/add-ons)

What I’m attaching: pricing_mapping_v1.xlsx (mapping examples) and marketplace_fee_matrix.pdf (public marketplace fee ranges). High level notes from our side below on unit price mapping and examples — please review and I’ll sync with Aditya to finalize numbers for the private offer draft.

High-level unit price mapping idea (summary):
- Redwood hosted list price (reference): $75 per 1M tokens (this is example list, not final)
- Marketplace private offer math: Marketplace unit_price = Redwood_unit_price * (1 + marketplace_fee_pct) + marketplace_surcharge_per_1M
- Typical marketplace_fee_pct we see: 5% - 15% depending on provider and negotiated terms; surcharge varies by marketplace and contract (see attached matrix)

Example mapping (using 1M token unit):
- Redwood list: $75/1M -> AWS Marketplace (12% fee) => ~$84/1M before any negotiated discount
- If we offer a 10% customer discount off Redwood list and factor AWS 12% => (75 * 0.9) * 1.12 = $75.6/1M
- Goal is to get you into the target effective unit we discussed: ~$80 - $100 per 1M tokens on marketplace depending on term/commitment

Next steps:
- Brian: confirm token run-rates & preferred marketplace routing by EOD Friday 10/31
- Aditya/Jonas: I’ve asked you to review the attached mapping and propose two private offer unit tiers (12-month and 24-month) we can present to procurement
- I’ll prep a draft private offer/DocuSign link once we confirm final unit tiers and term

Thanks — talk soon.

Adding detail on the example AWS mapping Brian requested. I ran quick numbers based on the 200M/mo baseline:

Assumptions (example):
- Redwood hosted list price: $75/1M tokens
- Negotiated customer discount (example tier): 10% for a 12-month commit; 18% for a 24-month commit
- AWS marketplace fee (example): 12% take on the final purchase price (typical commercial deal)
- We model unit in $/1M tokens for clarity

12-month example (200M/mo):
- List unit: $75/1M
- Customer discount 10% -> $67.50/1M
- AWS fee (12%) applied by marketplace to purchase price -> effective on-customer invoice math: $67.50 * 1.12 = $75.60/1M
- Monthly cost at 200M: 200 * $75.60 = $15,120 (note: 200M tokens equals 200 units of 1M)
- Annualized cost: $181,440

24-month example with deeper discount: 18%
- Discounted unit: $75 * 0.82 = $61.50/1M
- After AWS 12% fee: $61.50 * 1.12 = $68.88/1M
- Monthly cost at 200M: 200 * $68.88 = $13,776 -> annual $165,312

Notes and levers:
- If BrightCart targets an effective ~$85/1M on marketplace, the 12-month example is well below that; if procurement wants a sub-$80 target, the 24-month example or a slightly deeper one-off discount gets there.
- Marketplace-specific surcharges can add fixed cents per 1M; we should confirm with each marketplace team. GCP/Azure fee % will differ slightly (GCP often lower in some programs, Azure varies by offer type).
- We can also offer a blended model where support/observability add-ons are invoiced directly to avoid marketplace fees on those line items.

Aditya will prepare a clean one-page pricing table and a sample PO/DocuSign payload for Marissa to share with procurement.
